summary: Tailosk Linen & Uniform Services, Inc., a commercial laundry operator serving hospitals and hotels, licenses Voupourt Software, LLC's 'WashLoop' plant-management, RFID garment-tracking and route-dispatch software. The license runs 36 months from February 1, 2026 under a Software License Agreement dated January 15, 2026. The folder also holds an Order Form, a concurrent Side Letter, a Quality Agreement governing release acceptance, Amendment No. 1 (June 1, 2026), a parent guaranty from Voupourt Holdings, Inc., the pre-signing term sheet and two distractors. Four issues are planted. (1) The Agreement auto-renews for 36-month terms with a 30-day opt-out window. (2) Tailosk's Rejection Notice of the Production Release came after the Quality Agreement's 15-business-day window, measured from the delivery date recited in the Amendment. (3) A customer-data indemnity in the Side Letter becomes uncapped through the Agreement's cap carve-out for 'indemnification obligations under this Agreement'. (4) The Amendment's broadened 'Affiliate' definition turns the Agreement's affiliate-assignment exception into a right for Voupourt to assign to any acquirer, including a competitor.

issues.label: automatic renewal
issues.description: Section 9.2 of the Software License Agreement makes the Agreement renew automatically for successive 36-month Renewal Terms. The only way out is a non-renewal notice given not more than 180 days nor less than 150 days before the end of the then-current term, which is a 30-day window. Each Renewal Term locks Tailosk into another three years of fees of about $412,800 per year. This departs from the 12-month renewal terms in the Term Sheet (D7). The Order Form says nothing on renewal, so it does not cure the point, and the Term Sheet is non-binding. This is the single-clause issue.
detect_terms: not more than 180 days nor less than 150 days
issues.expected_finding: Section 9.2 auto-renews the Agreement for 36-month terms unless Tailosk gives notice in a narrow 30-day window 150 to 180 days before term end, contrary to the 12-month renewals in the Term Sheet, so Tailosk should seek 12-month renewals with a longer and simpler opt-out (or calendar the window) before the initial term ends.

issues.label: expired notice window
issues.description: Section 5.3 of the Quality Agreement lets Tailosk reject the Production Release, and recover the Implementation Fees, by Rejection Notice within fifteen Business Days after the Delivery Date. Otherwise the release is deemed accepted and Tailosk's remedy is limited to warranty re-performance. Read alone, this is an ordinary acceptance mechanic. Amendment No. 1, Recital B states that the Production Release was delivered on April 6, 2026, so the window closed on April 27, 2026. Recital C records Tailosk's Rejection Notice dated May 14, 2026, which is 13 business days late. Recital C also states that nothing in the Amendment waives Tailosk's rights in respect of the Rejection Notice, so Tailosk's objection is preserved and has not been accepted away. The Amendment prevails over the Quality Agreement but does not extend the window.
detect_terms: within fifteen (15) Business Days after the Delivery Date
issues.expected_finding: Measured from the April 6, 2026 delivery date in Amendment No. 1, the Quality Agreement's 15-business-day rejection window closed on April 27, 2026, so Tailosk's May 14, 2026 Rejection Notice is untimely and Licensor can treat the release as deemed accepted, cutting off the Implementation Fee refund. Tailosk should rely on the Amendment's non-waiver language and its warranty rights, and negotiate a written extension or reopening of the acceptance window.
detect_terms2: delivered the Production Release on April 6, 2026

issues.label: uncapped indemnity
issues.description: Section 12.3 of the Software License Agreement excludes from the Section 12.2 cap 'each party's indemnification obligations under this Agreement'. Within the Agreement, only Licensor gives an indemnity (the IP indemnity in Section 10.1), so the carve-out appears to favour Tailosk. Section 3 of the concurrent Side Letter (D5) has Tailosk defend, indemnify and hold harmless Licensor against all claims arising from Customer Data, including hospital-customer garment and patient-linen tracking data. Section 5 of the Side Letter says it is incorporated into and forms part of the Agreement, and Agreement Section 1.3 ranks Side Letters above the Agreement. Read alone, the Side Letter indemnity looks like it sits under the general cap. Read together, Tailosk's customer-data indemnity becomes an indemnification obligation under this Agreement and falls outside the cap. That exposes Tailosk to unlimited liability, including privacy and breach claims from its healthcare customers.
detect_terms: each party's indemnification obligations under this Agreement
issues.expected_finding: Because the Side Letter's Customer Data indemnity is incorporated into the Agreement, and Agreement Section 12.3 excludes all indemnification obligations under the Agreement from the 12-month-fees cap, Tailosk's customer-data indemnity to Licensor is uncapped. Tailosk should limit the Section 12.3 carve-out to Licensor's Section 10.1 IP indemnity, or expressly cap the Side Letter indemnity.
detect_terms2: shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Licensor

issues.label: unrestricted assignment
issues.description: Section 15.2 of the Software License Agreement bars assignment without the other party's prior written consent, except that either party may assign without consent to an Affiliate. Section 1.1 of the Agreement defines Affiliate in the usual control-based way, so the clause is protective on its own. Amendment No. 1, Section 2.1, restates 'Affiliate' for all purposes of the Agreement. The stated reason is to let Tailosk's newly acquired laundry plants use the software. The new definition covers entities under common control 'now or in the future' and any person that merges with a party or its parent or acquires a majority of its voting securities. Under Section 1.3 the Amendment prevails over the Agreement. Read together, Voupourt can assign the Agreement without Tailosk's consent to any acquirer of Voupourt or its parent. That includes a competing laundry operator or linen-management vendor, which would gain Tailosk's route, pricing and customer data.
detect_terms: may assign this Agreement without consent to an Affiliate
issues.expected_finding: The Amendment's expanded Affiliate definition, which includes any acquirer of a party or its parent and prevails under Section 1.3, turns Section 15.2's affiliate exception into a right for Voupourt to assign the license to any acquirer, including a Tailosk competitor, without consent. Tailosk should limit the expanded definition to its own permitted-user purposes and require consent (or a termination right) for any assignment by Licensor upon a change of control or to a competitor.
detect_terms2: acquires a majority of its voting securities
